# View templates (step 15)

Write every view **whole**, from `requirements.json`. Never patch one in place. The files in [views/](views/) are the exact expected output for the US-001 worked example. Copy their structure, headings, tables and marker comments; only the content changes per project.

**Header.** Every view starts with:

```markdown
# <View title> — <project.name>

> Generated from `requirements/requirements.json` (run <project.last_run>). Do not edit this file by hand[ except …]; change the JSON and regenerate.
```

`npm run verify` uses `(run <id>)` to detect a stale view.

**Origin badges** go after every requirement title: `**[Explicit]**`, `**[Inferred]**`, `**[Recommended]**`, `**[Unknown]**`.

**Internal items** (`client_visible: false`) never appear in `requirements.md` or `client-summary.md`. They still appear in `traceability.md`, `business-rules.md` and `risks.md`, marked `*(internal)*`.

**Deprecated items** appear only in `traceability.md`, and only when they are still referenced.

| File | Golden example | Content | Human-editable part |
|---|---|---|---|
| `requirements.md` | [views/requirements.md](views/requirements.md) | A summary table, then one section per type (FR, NFR, BR, DR, IR, SR, CR, CON, ASM, DEP). Each item shows its source, priority (marked proposed or confirmed), phase, status, client's words, rationale, metric, links, open questions, reason for its priority, design refs and Given/when/then criteria | **Sign-off table** at the end: one row per client-visible item |
| `client-summary.md` | [views/client-summary.md](views/client-summary.md) | For the client to read in two minutes: the problem, objectives, the MVP list, later phases, BLOCKING client questions, HIGH-impact risks, the top 5 ideas (clearly labelled *not requirements*) and next steps | none |
| `open-questions.md` | [views/open-questions.md](views/open-questions.md) | Client questions, then internal ones, each ordered BLOCKING → HIGH → NORMAL. Every question shows `### Q-### [URGENCY] text`, what it blocks, its options and the suggested default. Answered and withdrawn questions go at the end | none: answers come through chat or the JSON |
| `innovation-opportunities.md` | [views/innovation-opportunities.md](views/innovation-opportunities.md) | A table, then ideas grouped by level, each with value, fit, score breakdown, prerequisites, risks and technology | **Decision block** under each idea (format below) |
| `tech-trends.md` | [views/tech-trends.md](views/tech-trends.md) | A table with a verified column, then details with sources or the verification note | none |
| `risks.md` | [views/risks.md](views/risks.md) | The risk register, ordered by likelihood × impact | none |
| `business-rules.md` | [views/business-rules.md](views/business-rules.md) | Rules grouped by `rule_category`, each with the requirements it governs | none |
| `traceability.md` | [views/traceability.md](views/traceability.md) | A Mermaid dependency graph (arrows point to the item depended on; isolated items are listed as single nodes), a story → requirement matrix, and promoted items with their INN | none |
| `validation-report.md` | written by the gate | See `requirements-validation-gate/references/report-template.md` | none |

## Decision block format

The format is exact, because the read-back step parses it. Do not change the markers or the field labels.

```markdown
<!-- decision:INN-001 -->
**Decision:** PENDING
**Reason:**
**Decided by:**
**Date:**
<!-- /decision -->
```

## Sign-off table format

```markdown
| ID | Title | Current status | Decision | By | Date | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FR-001 | Book an appointment online | NEEDS_CLARIFICATION |  |  |  |  |
```

A human fills in `Decision` with `APPROVED` or `CHANGES`, plus `By` and `Date`. Leave those columns empty when you generate the table.
